summary.short: Requires institutions authorized by the Central Bank of Brazil to adopt a cybersecurity policy and incident response plan, and to meet conditions for relevant cloud and data processing contracts, including notice to and authorization by the central bank for overseas services. Effective 1 July 2021.
summary.long: Requires institutions authorized by the Central Bank of Brazil (BCB) to adopt a board-approved cybersecurity policy with minimum controls (Arts. 2–3-A) and an incident response plan (Art. 6). Policies are disclosed to staff and third-party providers, and a summary to the public (Arts. 4–5). Institutions designate a responsible director, file an annual report and review policies yearly (Arts. 7–10). Contracting of relevant data processing, storage and cloud computing services requires prior governance and provider checks (Art. 12) and notice to the BCB within ten days (Art. 15). For overseas services, institutions need an information-exchange agreement with the relevant supervisors or, absent one, BCB authorization requested at least sixty days in advance (Art. 16). Contracts must include minimum clauses on data location, segregation, subcontracting notice and BCB access (Art. 17). Business continuity, monitoring, incident information sharing and annual intrusion tests by independent parties follow (Arts. 19–22-A). The BCB may set further requirements (Art. 24) and may veto or restrict non-compliant contracts (Art. 26). Pre-2018 contracts had to be adapted within a deadline not exceeding 31 December 2021 (Art. 25). The text sets no monetary penalties.
